title: Krishna consciousness
hook: the name everyone calls them isn't their name. it's a line from their song
carry: krishna consciousness: keep krishna in mind
tomorrow: can someone not born Hindu belong at the Krishna feast?

segments.voice: Yesterday closed with sankirtana, God's names sung together, where the room answers the voice. Today, the people who took that singing out onto the sidewalk.

Saffron cloth, a drum on a strap, small brass cymbals, and a song with only a few words in it, going round and round on a city sidewalk. Passersby have a name ready: the Hare Krishnas. Here's the odd part. That isn't their name. It's a line from their song, turned into a nickname. Their real name is longer, and it hides a bigger puzzle about who Krishna is.
screen: `SAFFRON, A DRUM, BRASS CYMBALS.` → `A NICKNAME FROM A SONG.` → `WHO IS KRISHNA, FOR THEM?`

segments.voice: Their own name is the International Society for Krishna Consciousness, ISKCON for short. And the reason sits in a story. On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna drops his bow and won't fight. Krishna, his charioteer, talks him through it for seventeen chapters: duty, the self that never dies, work without clinging. Then, near the very end, he says: hear my most secret word. In paraphrase: fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, offer to me, bow to me, and you will come to me. Let go of every other duty and take refuge in me alone. Arjuna picks up his bow; his confusion, he says, is gone. For these devotees, that last word is the whole program: keep Krishna in mind, not only while singing, but while cooking, working, walking to the bus. Now the puzzle. Many Vaishnavas, devotees of Vishnu, honor Krishna as Vishnu come to earth. This lineage, from the Bengal saint Chaitanya, turns that around. After listing Vishnu's descents, the Bhagavata Purana says: these are portions, but Krishna is the Lord himself. So for them, Krishna is the source, Vishnu included. Other Hindus hold it differently: Advaita teachers speak of one reality beyond every form; devotees of Shiva or the Goddess place them at the center. This lineage's answer is Krishna, and the nickname from the song sits on top of it.
screen: `KURUKSHETRA: ARJUNA DROPS HIS BOW.` · `HEAR MY MOST SECRET WORD.` · `FIX YOUR MIND ON ME.` · `IN MIND WHILE COOKING, WORKING.` · `KRISHNA IS THE LORD HIMSELF.` · then, large: `KEEP KRISHNA IN MIND.`

segments.voice: Devotees chant while they do ordinary things. Pick up something you'll use later today, a cup, a pen, your keys, and hold it. Softly say the chant as you look at it: Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare; Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare. If you don't pray, say quietly what you'd like to keep in mind while you use it, and notice how often the mind wanders off.
The Hare Krishnas: a nickname from a song, for ISKCON, a Krishna-centered lineage with roots in Bengal.
Something to keep from Arjuna's chariot: Krishna consciousness, keeping Krishna in mind through every task. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Devotees in ISKCON temples chant the Hare Krishna mantra, study the Bhagavad Gita and try to offer their daily work, cooking and worship to Krishna.

chat.meaning: ISKCON is a Gaudiya Vaishnava lineage from Hindu Bengal, living Krishna's last word to Arjuna: fix your mind on me. For them Krishna is the source of all; other Hindus hold it differently. Some devotees prefer the old name sanatana dharma to the word Hindu.

ISKCON.meaning: International Society for Krishna Consciousness, the movement's own name

Chaitanya.meaning: the Bengal saint whose followers sang Krishna's names

Gaudiya Vaishnavas.meaning: the Krishna-devoted lineage with roots in Bengal

Advaita.meaning: the Vedanta school of one reality beyond name and form
